label: Contract result adverb
summary: Gives "poorly", "well" or "stellarly" for how a task contract's score turned out.
details: It compares the contract's score tally with the contract's first, second and third win thresholds: "poorly" at or below the first, "well" when equal to the second, "stellarly" when equal to the third. It reads the saved scope `scope:task_contract`, so that scope has to exist where the text is used.

label: Script topic
summary: Gives a short phrase naming a topic of conversation that matches the topic of a task contract.
details: It reads the contract's passage topic (diplomacy, martial, stewardship, intrigue or learning) from `scope:task_contract`; there are two phrases per topic and the game may pick either one. Some phrases fill in the culture of the character's current location or the name of the barony there, for example "the battle of <barony>". Only the first four texts are shown in the input; the other phrases follow the same keys.

label: Season
summary: Gives the name of the current season: spring, summer, autumn or winter.
details: It tests the current season. The list also has entries for the dry season and the rainy season (the rainy one twice, the second time with no condition at all). The input gives no texts for these, so what they print is unknown. The keys of the four season names start with "generatepoem_title".

label: Season adjective
summary: Gives a describing word for the current season: fresh (spring), sweltering (summer), humid (autumn) or cold (winter).
details: It tests the current season. The keys start with "generatepoem_title".

label: Follower trait line
summary: Gives one spoken line that matches a personality trait stored on the character.
details: The trait is the one saved in the character's variable `second_follower_trait_var`; there is one line per trait (callous, sadistic, zealous, craven and so on). All keys start with "ep3_camp_party.2000". The lines use emphasis marks around single words. The input shows only the first twelve entries (the game's documentation lists "lazy" twice).

label: Confessed crime
summary: Gives a phrase for a crime the character has a secret about, such as "committing murder" or "being a deviant".
details: Each entry applies when the character has a secret of one kind (murder, murder attempt, deviant, cannibal, incest, embezzlement and more), and the phrase uses that secret type's name. A fallback entry covers the rest.

label: Crime with article
summary: Gives a description of the character's secret crime that starts with "a".
details: Each entry applies when the character has a secret of one kind (murder, deviant, cannibal, incest and more). Its text is "a" followed by another text (for example `crime_murderer_desc`) that names that kind of criminal. A fallback entry covers the rest.

label: Servants word
summary: Gives "camp followers" if the character has the landless adventurer government, otherwise "servants".
details: The second entry is the fallback.

label: Opposite pronoun
summary: Gives the pronoun of the opposite gender: "he" for a female character, "she" for a male one.
details: The game also marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Shocked word
summary: Gives a word for a shocked reaction: "shocked" or "appalled".
details: Neither entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick, so either word can come out.

label: Shocked word (female)
summary: Gives one of two shocked-reaction words kept in separate "_female" entries.
details: Neither entry has a condition and the game marks it as valid for a random pick. The input shows no text for either entry, so the exact words are not known. Its name suggests it is the female version of the shocked-word text, but nothing checks the character's gender.

label: Simple color
summary: Gives a color name: blue, red, yellow, orange, cyan, purple, pink, grey or black.
details: No entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick, so any of the colors can come out.

label: Sin or misdeed
summary: Gives the game-concept link for "sin" if the character's religion is in the Abrahamic family, otherwise for "misdeed".
details: The check is on the character's religion family (`rf_abrahamic`).

label: Sinful or shameful
summary: Gives the concept link for "sinful" if the character's religion is in the Abrahamic family, otherwise for "shameful".
details: The check is on the character's religion family (`rf_abrahamic`).

label: Small food
summary: Gives the name of a small food item: "apple" or "biscuit".
details: Neither entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Small food with article
summary: Gives a small food item with its article: "an apple" or "a biscuit".
details: Neither entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Hiding object
summary: Gives the name of a piece of furniture: barrel, chest, cupboard, casket or cabinet.
details: The key's name calls these small hiding objects. No entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Cat sleeping spot
summary: Gives a phrase telling where cats sleep at a special building, such as "on top of the many altars".
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. The group of phrases that applies depends on the kind of travel point of interest the province's building has (religious, learning, economic and so on); there are three phrases per kind, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Diplomacy icon prefix
summary: Gives the diplomacy icon, or nothing.
details: It runs on a province. The icon shows when the game's check for a diplomacy-skill monument is true for the province; otherwise a blank text is used. Its key is named as a prefix, so it comes in front of a line about the building's diplomacy bonus.

label: Intrigue icon prefix
summary: Gives the intrigue icon, or nothing.
details: It runs on a province. The icon shows when the game's check for an intrigue-skill monument is true for the province; otherwise a blank text is used. Its key is named as a prefix, so it comes in front of a line about the building's intrigue bonus.

label: Learning icon prefix
summary: Gives the learning icon, or nothing.
details: It runs on a province. The icon shows when the game's check for a learning-skill monument is true for the province; otherwise a blank text is used. Its key is named as a prefix, so it comes in front of a line about the building's learning bonus.

label: Martial icon prefix
summary: Gives the martial icon, or nothing.
details: It runs on a province. The icon shows when the game's check for a martial-skill monument is true for the province; otherwise a blank text is used. Its key is named as a prefix, so it comes in front of a line about the building's martial bonus.

label: Special building name
summary: Gives the name of the special building (a wonder, holy site, mine, university and so on) in the province.
details: It runs on a province. It has 371 entries, one per special building; each applies when the province has that building, and its text points to the building type's name. A few keys appear twice in the list (the Liangzhe mines level 4, the Hetian mines level 1 and the Nalanda university).

label: Building legend
summary: Gives a made-up local legend about the province's special building, for example that the shadows inside it move of their own accord.
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. There are five legends for each kind of building (religious, learning, mines, martial, economic, diplomatic, ancient wonders, natural wonders), chosen by the building's travel point of interest; the game marks it as valid for a random pick. The text includes the building's name, with "the" in front where needed.

label: Building person
summary: Gives the title of a person who would be found at a special building, such as Cleric, Devotee, Acolyte or Pilgrim.
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. The roles depend on the kind of building (religious, learning, mines, martial, economic, diplomatic, ancient and natural wonders), and the game marks it as valid for a random pick. The input shows only the first four texts.

label: Building "the" prefix
summary: Gives "the " (with a space) in front of a special building's name, or nothing for a list of buildings whose name already carries it.
details: It runs on a province. The empty text is used when the province has one of a fixed list of buildings (for example the pyramids, the colosseum, Stonehenge or Notre Dame); every other building gets "the ". Other building texts put it in front of the name.

label: Building song verse
summary: Gives a short song verse about the province's special building.
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. The verses include the building's name, and there are three for each kind of building (religious, learning, mines, martial and so on); the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Stewardship icon prefix
summary: Gives the stewardship icon, or nothing.
details: It runs on a province. The icon shows when the game's check for a stewardship-skill monument is true for the province; otherwise a blank text is used. Its key is named as a prefix, so it comes in front of a line about the building's stewardship bonus.

label: Building surface
summary: Gives a phrase for a surface at a special building: a large flat rock, the mine entrance or a wall.
details: It runs on a province. The rock is used for a natural-feature building, the mine entrance for an economic one (except a few named buildings), and the wall for everything else. Each text includes the building's name.

label: Tourist building description
summary: Gives a visitor's diary-style description of a special building, one text per building.
details: It runs on a province. It has about 316 entries, each applying when the province has that building (or a higher level of it). The texts shown are first-person accounts of what the visitor sees.

label: Commons or square
summary: Gives "commons" if the character's location is a nomad, herder or tribal holding or a nomadic location, otherwise "square".
details: The second entry has no condition.

label: Stewardship building
summary: Gives the name "Manor Houses", the farm estates building.
details: The list has one entry only, marked as the fallback, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Stress desire
summary: Gives a first-person phrase for how a stressed character wants to cope, chosen by the stress-coping trait the character has.
details: There is one phrase per trait (drunkard, hashishiyah, rakish, reclusive, irritable, flagellant, profligate, improvident and more). Some phrases name the character's regional drink.

label: Study chance word
summary: Gives a word for the chance of success when studying a commander trait: very good, good, fair, poor, very poor or none.
details: The game compares the character's chance value with four limits (very good, good, fair, poor); "none" is the entry without a condition. Each word has its own text style, for example yellow for fair. The input shows only the first four texts.

label: Stump name
summary: Gives the word for what is left of a cut tree, such as "stump", "rump" or "lump", depending on the terrain of the character's location.
details: There is one entry per terrain (plains, hills, mountains, desert, jungle, forest, taiga and others) plus a fallback that gives "stump".

label: Follower or subject
summary: Gives "follower" for an adventurer's people, otherwise "subject".
details: "Follower" shows for a ruler with the landless adventurer government, or for a non-ruler whose liege has it. Everyone else gets "subject".

label: Heir motion
summary: Gives a phrase for how an heir takes over: "steps forward as leader" or "ascends to the throne".
details: The "leader" phrase is for a ruler with the landless adventurer government, for certain administrative non-independent rulers, for a ceremonial regent, or for a non-ruler whose liege is a landless adventurer. Everyone else gets "ascends to the throne".

label: Succession place note
summary: Gives a small note with the character's place in line for the second character's primary title, such as "(second in line)", or nothing.
details: The note shows when the character is at place 20 or better in the line of succession to the primary title of the saved scope `scope:second`; otherwise the empty text is used.

label: Succession place sentence
summary: Gives a sentence saying the character is a given place in line to your titles, or nothing.
details: The text says the character (as "she" or "he") is, for example, second in line, counted on the primary title of the saved scope `scope:second`. It shows when the place is 20 or better; otherwise the empty text is used.

label: Swan name
summary: Gives a name for a swan, such as Ill-Fated, Rose, Honky Honk or Honker.
details: There are nine names with no conditions, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick. The input shows only the first four texts.

label: Taltos term
summary: Gives "Táltos" if the character follows the Magyar religion, otherwise the general word "Mystic".
details: The second entry is the fallback.

label: Court position name
summary: Gives the name of a court position, such as royal architect, seneschal or court tutor.
details: The position is the one stored in the character's variable `target_court_position`. It has 41 entries, one per court position; each text asks the game for that position's name.

label: Court position duty
summary: Gives a short phrase about what a court position does, such as "managing the upkeep and expansion of your fine holdings".
details: The position is the one stored in the character's variable `target_court_position`. It has 41 entries, matching the court positions. The phrases speak to the ruler ("your holdings").

label: Contract tier name
summary: Gives the game-concept link for a task contract's tier, chosen by the character's government: governance issue, settlement issue or mandala ritual.
details: Administrative governments get the governance issue, nomadic ones the settlement issue and mandala ones the mandala ritual.

label: Dwelling or tavern
summary: Gives "dwelling" if the character's location is a nomad, herder or tribal holding or a nomadic location, otherwise "tavern".
details: The second entry has no condition.

label: Tribespeople or taverngoers
summary: Gives "tribes-people" if the character's location is a nomad, herder or tribal holding or a nomadic location, otherwise "tavern-goers".
details: The second entry has no condition.

label: Land type
summary: Gives a word for the kind of land in a province: wetland, farmland, grassland, scrubland, highland or woodland.
details: It runs on a province and the word depends on its terrain (for example farmland for farmlands and floodplains, woodland for forest and taiga). Hills match both the grassland and the highland entries. A fallback entry exists whose text the input does not show. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Murder scene by terrain
summary: Gives a story paragraph in which one entourage member kills another, with a method that fits the province's terrain.
details: It runs on a province. There is one text per terrain (desert, farmlands, forest, hills, jungle and more). The texts use the saved scopes `entourage_member_1` and `entourage_member_2` and name how each is related to the player. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Tree area
summary: Gives a word for a tree-covered area: forest, wood or jungle, depending on the province's terrain.
details: It runs on a province. Jungle is for jungle terrain; "wood" and "forest" both fit plains, hills, steppe, wetlands, forest and taiga, and "forest" is also the fallback for desert, oasis and floodplains. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Terrain name
summary: Gives the name of the province's terrain, such as plain, hill, jungle, wetland, floodplain, taiga, dryland or steppe.
details: It runs on a province and has one entry per terrain, more than the input shows. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Throat singing style
summary: Gives the name of a throat singing style (sygyt, hoomei or kargyraa), linked to its glossary entry.
details: The style is the one stored in the character's variable `throatsinging_style`.

label: Throne room name
summary: Gives the glossary link for the Chrysotriklinos if the character is a Roman emperor with the capital in province 496, otherwise the words "throne room".
details: The second entry is the fallback.

label: Title tier name
summary: Gives the name of a title's tier: Hegemony, Empire, Kingdom, Duchy, County or Barony.
details: It runs on a title and gives the name that matches the title's tier.

label: Title tier concept
summary: Gives the game-concept link for a title's tier (hegemony, empire, kingdom, duchy, county or barony).
details: It runs on a title. In the game the link can be hovered to see the concept's explanation.

label: Title tier plural
summary: Gives the plural name of a title's tier, such as Empires, Kingdoms or Duchies.
details: It runs on a title.

label: Ruler title (female)
summary: Gives the female ruler title for a title's tier, such as Empress, Queen or Duchess.
details: It runs on a title.

label: Ruler title (male)
summary: Gives the male ruler title for a title's tier, such as Emperor, King or Duke.
details: It runs on a title.

label: Title tier icon
summary: Gives the small icon for a title's tier.
details: It runs on a title. Each text is an icon code (for example the empire icon), not words.

label: Title tier adjective
summary: Gives a describing word for the rank of the character's highest title, such as imperial, royal, ducal, comital or baronial.
details: It runs on a character and goes by the highest title tier they hold. It also has rank words for steppe and tribal cases: khaganal and khanal (feudal, tribal, administrative or nomadic government with a Mongolic or Turkic heritage culture) and chiefly (tribal or steppe government). "Noble" is used for a character who is not lowborn, and "common" for the rest.

label: Top liege rite line
summary: Gives a tooltip line for the faith map mode: "Rite of Top Liege" followed by the rite's name.
details: It runs on a province. The line shows only when the county's holder has a top liege whose rite differs from the holder's own rite; the rite named is the top liege's. It has this one entry only.

label: Tourist arrival line
summary: Gives a line in a tourist's voice about arriving at a holding, such as "My excitement mounts as I near the <title>".
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. The text includes the name of the location's title. There are five entries for each holding type (castle, city, church and tribal) and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Tourist farewell line
summary: Gives a closing line in a tourist's voice about what the visit taught.
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. The entries are grouped by the kind of travel point of interest (learning or religious, diplomatic, martial, economic, wonder), and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Tourist exploring line
summary: Gives an excited line in a tourist's voice about starting to explore a site.
details: It runs on a province and saves it as `scope:location`. No entry has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Tournament favor
summary: Gives the word for a token carried into a tournament: glove, sleeve or scarf.
details: The choice follows the character's culture era as written in the script: glove for a culture in the early medieval era or later, sleeve for the late medieval era or later, and scarf as the always-true last entry.

label: Tournament prize line
summary: Gives a line for a tournament invitation about how good the prizes are, from mere baubles to splendid.
details: It follows the prizes option chosen for the tournament activity the character is involved in (bad, normal, good, very good or splendid). Each line is wrapped in line breaks.

label: Elder or town crier
summary: Gives "elder" if the character's location is a nomad, herder or tribal holding or a nomadic location, otherwise "town crier".
details: The second entry has no condition.

label: Elder or crier, capitalized
summary: Gives "Elder" or "Town Crier" in capital letters, chosen the same way as the lowercase version.
details: It gives the elder text when the character's location is a nomad, herder or tribal holding or a nomadic location, and "Town Crier" otherwise. The first entry reuses the text of the lowercase "elder" key, so its capital letter comes from where it is used.

label: Trade goods
summary: Gives a phrase for a bundle of trade goods, such as a set of furs or a handful of scented pouches.
details: None of the five entries has a condition, and the game marks it as valid for a random pick. One entry names a small animal for the meat, taken from another custom text.

label: Trees or scaffolding
summary: Gives "in the <tree> trees" or "the scaffolds".
details: The tree text is used when the game's check for a snowy rural Scandinavian location is true, and it names a tree that fits the character's current location. Any other case gives "the scaffolds".

label: Tribal or feudal
summary: Gives "Tribal" if the character's government is tribal, otherwise "Feudal".
details: Any government that is not tribal gives "Feudal".

label: Reform target government
summary: Gives the word "clan" or "feudal" for the government a tribal reform leads to.
details: "Clan" is given when the game's clan-inclined check is true for the character: their faith belongs to Islam, or their culture has an Arabic, Iranian or Turkic heritage. Otherwise "feudal".

label: Tribal trade goods
summary: Gives a pair of trade goods typical for the region of the character's location, such as furs and birch bark vessels in the north or spices and colorful textiles in India.
details: The regions are northern Europe, India, Africa, the steppe and the coast of Asia, plus a generic entry for every other place.

label: Tribalize or feudalize
summary: Gives "Tribalize" if the character's government is tribal, otherwise "Feudalize".
details: Any government that is not tribal gives "Feudalize".

label: Gift description
summary: Gives a phrase for a gift at the Tsagaan Sar festival, such as "some coin", "a satchel of gold" or "a small chest of gold", and entries for livestock.
details: The gift item and its size are read from the character's variables `tsagaan_sar_gift_item` and `tsagaan_sar_gift_amount` (miniscule, minor, medium and so on); the gold phrases grow larger down the list. The list also has livestock entries (a flock, a horse, sheep, cattle). The game marks it as valid for a random pick. The list has more entries than the input shows.

label: Rebellion color
summary: Gives a color name for the Turban rebellion: Red, Green, White, Black or Yellow.
details: The color follows the Wu Xing element stored in the dynastic cycle situation: metal gives red, earth green, wood white, fire black and water yellow. It is defined for any scope (the game's documentation gives none).

label: Tutor education
summary: Gives the name of the character's education focus: War, Stewardship, Diplomacy, Intrigue or Learning.
details: It goes by which education trait the character has. The first entry (martial education) points to the war concept.

label: Unbeliever or foreigner term
summary: Gives a word for how the character sees the second character: infidel, heathen or heretic, with "foreign" in front when their cultures differ, or "believer".
details: The game's infidel, heathen and heretic checks run with the saved scope `scope:second` as the one judged and the character as the one judging. The three "foreign" entries also need different cultures and come first; the "believer" entry is the fallback.

label: Unbeliever name
summary: Gives "heathen" if the character's faith has the pagan hostility doctrine, otherwise "infidel".
details: It describes someone of another faith as seen from the character's own faith.

label: Unbeliever name plural
summary: Gives "heathens" if the character's faith has the pagan hostility doctrine, otherwise "infidels".
details: It is the plural of the unbeliever name.

label: Unbeliever term
summary: Gives a word for how the character sees the second character: infidel, heathen, heretic or the general "unbeliever".
details: The game's infidel, heathen and heretic checks run with the saved scope `scope:second` as the one judged and the character as the one judging; "unbeliever" is the last entry, always true.

label: Unbeliever adjective
summary: Gives the describing word that matches how the character sees the second character: infidel, heathen, heretical or unbelieving.
details: It uses the same checks on `scope:second` as the unbeliever term; "unbelieving" is the last entry, always true.

label: Upper clothing
summary: Gives a word for an upper garment: "shirt" for a character who is not female, "blouse" or "dress" for a female one.
details: The game marks it as valid for a random pick, so the female entries (blouse, dress) can be chosen between.

label: Upper clothing adjective
summary: Gives the adjective entry that matches the upper garment words (shirt for a non-female character, blouse or dress for a female one).
details: The input shows no text for any of the three entries, so the exact words are not known. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Knights header
summary: Gives a heading for the list of people who can be knights: "Eligible followers" for an adventurer's people, or "Eligible courtiers and vassals" otherwise.
details: The first heading is used for a ruler with the landless adventurer government, or for a non-ruler whose liege has it. The second is the fallback.

label: Contest ending line
summary: Gives a sentence about how a one-on-one tournament contest ended, for jousting, wrestling, dueling or a board game.
details: The kind of contest is the current phase of the activity the character is in, with three sentences each; the game marks it as valid for a random pick. The sentences name the winner (the character) and the other character (`second`), for example who unhorsed whom.

label: Contest tool
summary: Gives a word for what is used in a versus contest: lance or horse, hands or steps, blade or weapon, hand or piece.
details: It runs on an activity and goes by the activity's current phase: joust gives lance or horse, wrestling hands or steps, duel blade or weapon, board game hand or piece. The game marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Contest phase
summary: Gives the name of a contest phase: Quarter Final, Semi-Final or Final.
details: It runs on an activity and reads the variable `contest_versus_progress`: 0 gives Quarter Final, 1 Semi-Final, 2 Final.

label: Contest round
summary: Gives the name of a tournament round: Quarter-Finals, Semi-Finals or Final.
details: It runs on an activity and reads the variable `contest_versus_progress`: 0, 1 or 2. The first entry's key says "qualifiers" but its text is "Quarter-Finals".

label: Victim or "my"
summary: Gives either the character's titled first name in the possessive form or the word "my".
details: The titled name is used when the character's top liege has the character flag `concerned_exists`; otherwise "my". A comment in vanilla says it is used in Hold Court.

label: Victim flag
summary: Gives one of two flag entries, "pt_true" or "pt_false", that tell whether the victim is meant.
details: "pt_true" is used when the character's top liege has the character flag `concerned_exists`, "pt_false" otherwise. The input shows no text for either entry, so what they print is not known. A comment in vanilla says the related text is used in Hold Court.

label: Chariot winning move
summary: Gives a sentence saying the character grips the reins and urges the horses to take the curve as tightly as possible.
details: There is one entry only and it has no condition; its key says it is the cut-off at the turn.

label: Wanderer lifestyle note
summary: Gives a note about the wanderer lifestyle: a bonus of extra experience from the traveler trait, or a list of unlocked activities.
details: A character with the traveler lifestyle trait gets the experience bonus note, which states how much more experience they gain. A landless adventurer without it sees the unlocked activities (hike and monument expedition); everyone else sees those plus the inspection activity.

label: Diarch appointment warning
summary: Gives a weak warning line, with a warning icon, about the succession problem of making a courtier diarch.
details: The warnings apply when the liege has a succession candidate with a higher diarchy score than the character and a courtly vassal exists. There is one warning for each problem: unrelated or related lowborn, and low, medium or high succession score. The related-lowborn entry contains `always = no`, so it can never show. An empty entry exists for no warning.

label: Weak diarch warning
summary: Gives a weak warning line, with a warning icon, about the diarch's succession score.
details: It shows when the character's liege has a diarchy succession candidate with a higher regent succession score than the character.

label: Wicked or dangerous
summary: Gives the concept link for "wicked" if the character's religion is in the Abrahamic family, otherwise for "dangerous".
details: The check is on the character's religion family (`rf_abrahamic`).

label: Liege relation title
summary: Gives how the character's role under their liege is written in a petition: council title, held positions, title as name, or "courtier".
details: A councillor gets the council title, a character with a court position gets the list of held court and council positions, a playable character gets their title as a name, and everyone else gets "courtier".

label: Wager type
summary: Gives a chariot wager type: win, place or show.
details: The type is the one stored in the character's variable `wager_type`.

label: Woman, man, girl or boy
summary: Gives the word woman, man, girl or boy for the second character.
details: It looks at the saved scope `scope:second`: an adult female gives "woman", an adult male "man", a non-adult female "girl" and a non-adult male "boy". The age checks also compare their age with the character's age with a margin of 20 years.

label: Woman or man, opposite
summary: Gives the word of the opposite gender: "man" for a female character, "woman" for a male one.
details: The game also marks it as valid for a random pick.

label: Women or men by faith
summary: Gives "men" or "women", depending on which gender is dominant in the character's faith.
details: "Men" applies when men are dominant or equal, "women" when women are dominant or equal. The game also marks it as valid for a random pick.
